summary: Inceptive I permits bare activity predicates (Hors 2/41; 11/211), d- clauses (94/248), b- activity nominals (11/147), and l- event expressions (60/96,176; 63/166). The occurrences do not establish separate meanings for each activity-complement form.

Personal b- target and b- activity coexist in MAC NI death and newlyweds/14 and 64/252. Subsense 1b captures the recurrent verbal-attack construction; conventionality beyond these contexts remains an editor question.
Overt l-marked participants occur with human actors (JTM 4.4/20; 92/43) and weather (91/9); this is not evidence for Detransitive. The entry shows no supported new stem or Detransitive.

Bədena (JTM 2.8/1) is unprefixed Infectum with joint-procedure force. kәbdela (Lahdo The snake/7) supports a ko-Preterit box by its bdela base; Bdéwalle supports Preterit-wa. Infectum-wa examples preserve the edition’s English rather than being translated into German.

The supplied compact records omit verse text and translations. Their reported classifications are retained provisionally with rejected_analysis audit flags; no independent source check or example publication is possible for them.

11/291 and 63/18 have following Preterit predicates; Talay 1/220 places bdeli after komhalaxno. These merit study of clause linkage rather than new senses. Talay 1/164 is interrupted and is not suitable as a complete example.

Round 2 only. Jan English is project machine translation, retained verbatim in selected excerpts; semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo. Round-1 proposals are retained as the baseline and are not repeated in this JSON.

Round 1 already introduced Preterit-wa and ko-Preterit; the readers' absent-box statements are stale. This round fills the Preterit-wa cell, adds an Imperativ and proposes a causative III from overt mabdewole.

Bare finite, d-clause, b- event noun, bare event object and source-point complements all retain begin I.1. Beginning with Jan as first interviewee (Jan 4.I/605) is ordering of an activity, not hostile personal b-.
Jan 1.16/693 bu təwqiḏo is firing of a kiln, not a new lexical sense of bdy; the interrupted ripening clause in Jan 1.17/907 adds no independently complete example.
Is the recurrent b- personal-target frame a conventional expression for berating, or productive ellipsis of beginning hostile speech? No physical assault is inferred.
Confirm the segmentation k- + bdela in Lahdo The snake/7 and the function of veǧa.
Check printed bdalla with the girls at 63/166, and gdobən at 94/92 against gbodən at 94/98; neither is silently emended.

Is mbadewole (Jan 2.31/5101) an II initiation form, a reduced causative related to mabdewole, or bdl? Its proposed stem is withheld.
Confirm III mabdewole (Jan 3.13/123) and elicit Preterit/Infectum base forms; only Preterit-wa is attested here.

Spatial beginning of the lunette/vault in MAC Ishaq Material culture/52,75 extends the same onset meaning to an architectural part. Non-agentive subjects also include ice, tape, famine and winter; l-series morphology alone does not imply a volitional actor.
Jan independently supports round-1 personal-target b- with berating embedded in a larger hostile treatment sequence; the existing gloss's gegen jdn. loslegen covers it.
Market spatial starting point supports round-1 spatial-onset extension; famine, construction, winter period and migration supply non-agentive event subjects, including l-marked ones.
